findings.summary: The new AUDIENCE_WORDS constant clashes by name with an existing constant in outcome.rs.
findings.evidence: outcome.rs:80 already defines `pub(super) const AUDIENCE_WORDS: [&str; 7]` (team, everyone, colleagues, customers, stakeholders, readers, public). reading.rs re-exports both modules with globs (`pub use outcome::*;` and `pub use surveys::*;`), and every child module does `use super::*`. A second `AUDIENCE_WORDS` in surveys.rs makes the glob re-exports ambiguous. That triggers the warn-by-default lint `ambiguous_glob_reexports`, which `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` (criterion 8) turns into an error. It also contradicts Decision 4, which rejected a new noun list because duplicates drift. Fix: Give the new list a distinct name, such as `CLARITY_AUDIENCE`, and say in its doc comment how it differs from `outcome::AUDIENCE_WORDS`. Or reuse the existing constant for its shared word (`readers`) and add only the persona-like words.

findings.summary: The clarity tier treats 'reader' and 'audience' as audience words, but both are also names of Athena's own roles.
findings.evidence: The reader role is named throughout briefs.rs and reading.rs, and `athena audience` is a role (audience.rs, main.rs:146). A plausible code request such as 'Make the verifier report clear to the reader' has a VISIBLE_NOUNS word ('report'), a clarity phrase and an audience word on one line. It would be refused, which goes against criterion 6. A Grep of HISTORY.txt found no past subject with this shape, so the risk is low, but it is the common-word false positive the soundness check asks about. Fix: In the clarity tier, accept 'reader' only with a qualifier: 'new reader', 'first-time reader', 'any reader' or 'a reader who'. Drop bare 'audience'. Add an Accept corpus case for 'Make the verifier report clear to the reader'.

findings.summary: Work items raised by the audience role, which are the clearest example of subjective-quality work, do not trigger the check, and no test pins that choice.
findings.evidence: `audience::work_item` sets the title to 'A {audience} rated {target} {n}/5; address its findings'. `approve_request` puts that title on the request's first line, which is not a generated line. `plain_line` drops the URL and the `3/5;` token because both contain '/', leaving 'A newcomer rated address its findings'. That line has no VISIBLE_NOUNS word, so the check accepts the reading whatever its criteria say. The plan says audience.rs is 'not a reading check' and does not look at this path through `athena go` into `check_reading_acceptance`. Fix: Add a corpus case built from `audience::work_item` plus the `approve_request` shape, and decide explicitly whether it should be refused (for example by also treating 'rated' next to a newcomer persona as a trigger) or accepted. State that decision as a known limit in the doc comment.
findings.location: Dependents: 'audience role that rates a live page as a newcomer'; crates/athena-core/src/audience.rs:98-116; crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs:279-299

findings.summary: The 5% share is labelled an estimate but has no stated basis.
findings.evidence: The sibling doc comment for `check_outcome_state` (outcome.rs:310-313) gives its basis: '29 of the 1045 recorded requests contain one of the four words'. The new doc comment states 5% with no reasoning. The producer cannot count records, because the snapshot has none. Fix: Have the doc comment and the changelog say how the 5% was estimated, for example from how many HISTORY.txt subjects hold the trigger phrases (the critic's Grep found none). Or say plainly that it is an upper-bound guess with no data behind it.
findings.location: Criterion 6 demonstration; step 4 doc comment ('expected 5% share is an estimate')

findings.summary: The plan overstates what `check_criteria_evidence` does: it does not make a Behavior criterion name a command.
findings.evidence: surveys.rs:91-114 only refuses criteria that cite producer evidence (`producer_evidence_phrase`). It does not require the criterion to name a command. Fix: Drop that claim, or say the method criterion names `athena audience` by convention, not because a check enforces it.

summary: Round-3 plan, checked against the snapshot with Read and Grep. I found no blocker or major problem. The plan puts the fix where the fault starts: one `step!` line added to the end of `refusing_check` (checks.rs:529-542). Adding it after `check_reading_references` leaves every pinned neighbour in place. I read `defined_terms_has_one_step_line_after_environment_reach`, `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` and the `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchor, and all three still hold. The plan reuses helpers that exist: `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189), `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39), `VISIBLE_NOUNS` (outcome.rs:49), `refuser_for` and `terms_reading` (reading.rs:6609-6618), `reading_source` (refusal_corpus.rs:2114), and `INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 41]` (refusal_corpus.rs:90). This job's own request does not trip the new check, because `ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR` (terms.rs:52) is present, so the generated Cause, Failure class and Introspection lines are dropped. The defaults.toml outcome-check sentence (line 89) meets all four parts of the matcher as specified: 'fresh model reader', 'as a newcomer', '4 of 5' and 'below 4'. The demonstrations call the production `refusing_check`, use no test doubles, and would fail without the step line. I found four minor problems. First, a new `AUDIENCE_WORDS` constant would clash with the existing `outcome::AUDIENCE_WORDS` through reading.rs's `pub use outcome::*; pub use surveys::*;`, which risks a clippy failure and repeats the duplicate list the plan itself rejected. Second, 'reader' and 'audience' are also names of Athena's own roles, so they can match where no person is meant. Third, audience-raised work items are not covered by the trigger, and no test pins that choice. Fourth, the 5% estimate has no stated basis.
